overview: Equifax is one of the three major U.S. consumer credit reporting bureaus (alongside Experian and TransUnion), operating a data and analytics business built on proprietary consumer, commercial, and employment/income records. The company has diversified beyond traditional credit reporting into employment and income verification through its Workforce Solutions segment, which now generates the largest share of profit and is anchored by The Work Number database. Equifax operates globally through three segments -- Workforce Solutions, U.S. Information Solutions (USIS), and International (Canada, Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific) -- serving lenders, employers, government agencies, and consumers.

business_model.summary: Equifax monetizes proprietary data assets (credit files, employment/income records, commercial data) through transaction-based and subscription-based products sold to banks, mortgage lenders, employers, government agencies, and consumers. Workforce Solutions (verification services plus HR/employer business-process-outsourcing) is the highest-margin, fastest-growing segment and is heavily levered to U.S. mortgage origination and hiring/gig-economy volumes. USIS sells credit reporting, scoring, identity/fraud, and decisioning products largely tied to consumer lending and mortgage activity. International replicates USIS-like products across Canada, Latin America (including Boa Vista in Brazil), Europe, and Asia Pacific.

revenue_streams.name: International
revenue_streams.trend: growing via M&A (Boa Vista, Circulo de Credito)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2B2C -- banks and mortgage lenders, employers/HR platforms, government agencies (background/verification), plus direct-to-consumer credit monitoring
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily U.S. (Workforce Solutions and USIS are almost entirely U.S.), with International spanning Canada, Latin America (Brazil via Boa Vista, Mexico via pending Circulo de Credito), UK/Europe, and Asia Pacific

competitive_position.market_position: One of the 'Big Three' U.S. credit bureaus (Experian is generally regarded as the largest by revenue); dominant, difficult-to-replicate leader in U.S. income/employment verification via The Work Number

moat_factors.description: 209M+ active employment records (813M+ total) sourced from ~4.9M employers/payroll providers under exclusivity arrangements; employers contribute data for free in exchange for offloading verification-request burden, creating low churn and a network effect that widens as more employers/payroll providers onboard

moat_factors.factor: Proprietary data scale and regulatory embedding
moat_factors.description: Credit files and verification data are deeply embedded in regulated lending, hiring, and tenant-screening workflows, creating high switching costs for financial institutions and HR platforms
Three-player U.S. credit bureau structure limits new entrants at the core reporting business, though verification niches face more competition (e.g., Argyle, Truework)

moat_factors.factor: EFX Cloud / data fabric technology platform
moat_factors.description: ~$3B multi-year cloud/security transformation (now largely complete) built a unified data fabric ingesting ~20B records/month and enabling faster, AI-embedded product development -- a scale advantage smaller rivals may struggle to match

weaknesses: USIS and Workforce Solutions Verification revenue are highly correlated with U.S. mortgage origination volumes, a deeply cyclical and currently depressed end market
Reputational overhang from the 2017 data breach persists in brand perception and invites continued regulatory scrutiny
Talent Solutions/hiring-related verification exposed to a soft U.S. labor market (job growth of only ~50-60k/month as of late 2026)
Heavy dependence on U.S. revenue concentrates macro and rate risk relative to more globally diversified peers

growth_drivers: Workforce Solutions Verification Services growth via record additions to The Work Number, new products (e.g., TWN Income for mortgage qualification), and expanding penetration in government and I-9/onboarding services
Non-mortgage diversification within Workforce Solutions -- Talent Solutions, Consumer Lending, and government verification posting double-digit growth even while mortgage-tied volumes are volatile

Bolt-on M&A: 14 acquisitions totaling more than $4.1 billion over the trailing ~24 months, including Boa Vista Servicos (Brazil's #2 credit bureau, completed Aug-2023) and pending Circulo de Credito (Mexico), expanding International's data footprint in Latin America
EFX Cloud/data-fabric platform substantially complete, enabling faster new-product launches (54 AI-embedded products launched in H1 2026) and a doubled AI-driven cost-reduction target of $150 million
Eventual U.S. mortgage/housing market normalization (lower rates) would be a strong cyclical tailwind given elevated operating leverage in Workforce Solutions Mortgage and USIS
Government contract wins (~$300 million in new/renewed annual contract value signed in H1 2026, benefiting 2027+)

business.description: Workforce Solutions Mortgage and USIS revenue are directly tied to U.S. mortgage origination and refinancing volumes; 30-year rates near 6.6-7% have caused housing activity to fall roughly 50% versus prior periods as of September 2026
Weak U.S. job growth (~50-60k/month) pressures Talent Solutions and onboarding/verification transaction volumes
Niche verification challengers (e.g., Argyle, Truework) and alternative payroll-data aggregators could erode The Work Number's exclusivity advantage over time
Large banks and mortgage lenders represent concentrated demand; pricing/volume negotiating leverage sits with a relatively small number of large financial institution customers

financial.description: Total debt of roughly $5.3-6.2B against EBITDA of ~$1.8-1.9B reflects sustained leverage from a heavy bolt-on acquisition strategy
International segment (Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific) creates reported-currency volatility; company has flagged FX as swinging full-year guidance by tens of millions of dollars

regulatory.risk: Legacy 2017 data breach liabilities and oversight
regulatory.description: Global settlement (up to $700M with FTC/CFPB/50 states) remains in claims-administration phase with free identity-restoration services running through January 2029; heightened data-security regulatory scrutiny persists
CFPB and state-level scrutiny of credit reporting accuracy, furnisher practices, and use of alternative data (medical debt, rental data) could constrain product design or monetization

Expanding U.S. state privacy laws and international regimes (GDPR-style rules) raise compliance costs and could restrict certain data uses, especially in Workforce Solutions and cross-border data transfer

macro.description: Mortgage rates are the single largest swing factor for both USIS and Workforce Solutions Mortgage revenue; elevated-for-longer rates directly compress the highest-margin part of the business
A broader credit slowdown or recession would reduce lending-related transaction volumes across USIS and International
Verification and Talent Solutions volumes scale with hiring activity, which has slowed materially through 2026

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Long-term structural growth in data/analytics and verification services, but near-term (2026) growth is being suppressed by a historically weak U.S. mortgage origination market and soft hiring; management still targets ~10% constant-currency organic growth for FY2026 driven by non-mortgage Workforce Solutions lines and M&A
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for the mortgage/USIS-linked portion of revenue; more resilient/secular for core credit reporting subscriptions and government/verification contracts
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High -- mortgage rates are a first-order driver of both revenue mix and reported growth quarter to quarter
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Moderate; International segment (Brazil, Mexico pending, Canada, Europe, Asia Pacific) creates translation risk, partially offset by local-currency growth reporting
key_input_costs: Labor/compensation for data science and product development

recent_developments.event: Revenue of $1.70B, up 11% reported / 10% local currency; adjusted EPS of $2.25 beat consensus ($2.20), but shares fell roughly 7-8.5% pre-market on weaker-than-expected guidance for Q3 and FY2026
Signed agreement to acquire Circulo de Credito (Mexican credit bureau); doubled AI-driven cost-reduction target to $150 million; returned $366 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends

Workforce Solutions grew revenue 7%, with Mortgage up ~8% (moderating from a stronger Q1) and Talent Solutions/Consumer Lending posting high-double-digit growth within Diversified Markets; Workforce Solutions EBITDA margin of 52.1%

Strong quarter aided by better-than-expected U.S. mortgage activity early in the quarter and new products (TWN Income); maintained full-year guidance midpoint of ~10% constant-currency growth despite acknowledging mortgage-market deceleration risk from higher rates
Company/management commentary flagged that U.S. housing-market activity had fallen roughly 50% versus prior periods as mortgage rates near 7% suppressed new-purchase and refinance volumes
Workforce Solutions Government signed new contract wins/renewals totaling ~$300 million in annual contract value, benefiting 2027 and beyond

Company neared completion of its multi-year cloud/security/data transformation, launching 54 new AI-embedded products in H1 2026 on the unified data fabric (processing ~20 billion records/month, with a reported 6 billion global online transactions in a single month)
2017 data breach settlement remains in claims-administration phase; free identity-restoration services for affected consumers continue through January 2029

items.vs_prior: lowered vs. original guidance midpoint of $6.72B / ~10.5% growth issued in February 2026; the reported-basis range was held roughly unchanged from April guidance
items.notes: Midpoint (~$6.75B) came in well below the analyst consensus of ~$7.39B at the time, driven by a sharper-than-expected mortgage market slowdown; constant-currency organic growth still guided near 10%

items.vs_prior: new guidance, midpoint below consensus of ~$1.71B
items.notes: Reflects continued mortgage-market weakness into H2 2026

items.vs_prior: Q3 EPS midpoint of $2.20 fell short of Street's ~$2.27 estimate
items.notes: April 2026 guidance raised full-year reported revenue by $25M and adjusted EPS by $0.04 for FX; by July, FX tailwind offset the Q2 beat, leaving reported guidance effectively unchanged even as constant-currency guidance was nudged up
Management cited AI-embedded product development and internal automation on the EFX Cloud data fabric as the source of incremental savings

items.target: High single-digit to low double-digit range (segment-level, qualitative)
items.vs_prior: maintained, with mix shifting toward non-mortgage lines (Talent Solutions, Consumer Lending, Government) as mortgage decelerates
items.notes: Segment EBITDA margins around 52% in Q2 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Management maintained a full-year constant-currency growth outlook near 10% even as it lowered/held reported revenue guidance below prior Street expectations, attributing the gap primarily to a sharper mortgage-market downturn (rates near 6.6-7%, housing activity down roughly 50% from prior periods as of mid-September 2026). Management emphasized outperformance in non-mortgage Workforce Solutions lines (Talent Solutions, Consumer Lending, Government), continued momentum in Latin America M&A integration (Boa Vista, pending Circulo de Credito), and the near-completion of the multi-year Equifax Cloud/data-fabric transformation as key offsets and long-term differentiators.

bull_case: The Work Number's scale (200M+ active records, ~4.9M contributing employers under exclusivity) is a genuinely hard-to-replicate data moat that continues to compound as more payroll providers and employers onboard

Non-mortgage Workforce Solutions lines (Talent Solutions, Consumer Lending, Government) are growing at high-single to double-digit rates and are diversifying the business away from pure mortgage cyclicality
A substantially complete multi-year cloud/data-fabric transformation should support faster AI-embedded product launches, margin expansion, and a doubled $150 million cost-reduction target

Eventual mortgage-rate normalization would be a powerful multi-year tailwind given how depressed current origination/refinance volumes are relative to history, creating significant operating leverage upside
Disciplined bolt-on M&A (Boa Vista, pending Circulo de Credito) is extending the data-moat playbook into large, underpenetrated Latin American credit markets
bear_case: Revenue and earnings remain highly levered to the U.S. mortgage cycle; a 'higher for longer' rate environment (mortgage rates near 7%, housing activity down ~50%) directly compresses the highest-margin segments (USIS and Workforce Solutions Mortgage)

FY2026 guidance was cut well below prior Street expectations (revenue midpoint ~$6.75B vs. consensus ~$7.39B), and shares sold off 7-8.5% on the Q2 2026 print despite an EPS beat, signaling the market is skeptical of the growth algorithm near-term
Soft U.S. hiring (job growth of only ~50-60k/month) pressures Talent Solutions and onboarding-related verification volumes just as mortgage is also weak, removing a hoped-for offset

Legacy reputational and regulatory overhang from the 2017 data breach persists (claims administration and consumer identity-restoration commitments run through January 2029), keeping the company a target for continued privacy/data-security regulation
Leverage from an aggressive bolt-on M&A strategy (~$4.1B across 14 deals in ~24 months) leaves the balance sheet more levered heading into a period of cyclical revenue softness
